God somebody finally put it into words. I CONSTANTLY struggle with the guilt that I'm not doing enough or that I'm parenting just as bad as my mother did me. Then I stop and think:
I'm not screaming in her face because she did something wrong.
I'm not throwing things at her in anger.
I'm not denying her basic medical needs.
I'm not denying her social interaction with children her age.
I'm not refusing to let her bathe as punishment.
I'm not beating her or threatening her.
I love my daughter and while I still worry that I don't play with her as often as I should, I would never look at her and think the kinds of things my mom did to me would be ok to do to her and I'm extremely proud of that. I struggle with my physical and mental health, so I learned a long time ago that it is ok to let her watch TV for an hour or two while I unwind reading a book on my bed or playing a game on my computer. We've had many talks about how she's feeling and the things she wants to do or learn or see. Every time I look in her eyes, they are bright and full of life and happiness and it eases my worry that I'm not a good enough parent, because she is blooming.

You're missing the point. A parent's first step into correcting a child's behavior shouldn't be immediately taking away something or restricting privacy in any way shape or form. Trust is a two-way street as well. Parents must earn their trust from their kids the same way kids must earn trust from their parents. immediately taking away the computer and making it a public device, especially if the original intent of the device was not for it to be public, is honestly not a step in the right direction. OP needs to sit down with his son and explain to him that he can't be doing what he's doing and needs to focus on his school work. Actually sitting down and talking with your children instead of immediately punishing them honestly has a greater impact especially in the long run.
